title: Access control policy
description: Define access control rules based on least privilege and need-to-know, covering systems that hold personal data.

title: Joiner, mover and leaver access process
description: Grant access on approved requests, adjust it on role change, and remove it within 24 hours of exit.

title: Multi-factor authentication
description: Enforce MFA for identity provider, cloud consoles, source code, email and all remote or administrative access.

title: Privileged access management
description: Limit admin and root access to named individuals, protect root accounts with MFA, and log privileged activity.

title: Periodic access reviews
description: Review user access to critical systems quarterly and remove access that is no longer needed.

title: Least privilege access to data
description: Restrict access to production data and personal data to roles that need it, enforced through role-based access.

title: Source code access
description: Restrict write and admin access to source code repositories and review it periodically.

title: Password and secrets management
description: Enforce strong password rules, use a password manager, keep secrets out of code, and scan repositories for leaked secrets.

title: Asset inventory
description: Maintain an inventory of hardware, software, cloud resources and information assets, each with an owner.

title: Acceptable use
description: Publish acceptable use rules for company systems and data, acknowledged by staff.

title: Information classification and handling
description: Classify information (for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Personal data) with labelling and handling and transfer rules for each level.

title: Media handling and secure disposal
description: Securely wipe or destroy media and equipment before disposal or re-use, and keep disposal certificates.

title: Endpoint security
description: Manage laptops and mobile devices with MDM, full-disk encryption, screen lock, OS updates and endpoint protection.

title: Protection of records
description: Protect business records from loss, tampering and unauthorised access, and keep them for the required retention periods.

title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
description: Maintain a business continuity and DR plan with RTO and RPO targets, keep security in place during disruption, and test the plan annually.

title: Encryption at rest and key management
description: Encrypt databases, storage volumes, backups and object storage at rest, with managed keys and documented key rotation.

title: Cyber Crisis Management Plan
description: Keep a Board-approved Cyber Crisis Management Plan covering detection, containment, response and recovery for cyber scenarios, aligned with CERT-In guidance, tested through drills or tabletop exercises at least yearly.

title: Independent annual IS and cyber security audit
description: Have qualified, independent auditors (CERT-In empanelled where the regulator requires) audit information systems and cyber security at least yearly, report to the Board or its committee, submit reports to the regulator when required, and track findings to closure.

title: Customer authentication for payments and sensitive changes
description: Require multi-factor authentication (with at least one dynamic factor) for payments, new beneficiaries, limit changes and changes to contact details, use risk-based or adaptive checks, lock accounts after repeated failures and protect sessions against hijacking.

title: Customer transaction alerts
description: Alert customers instantly for every debit, credit and sensitive account change, show the actual merchant name, mask account and card numbers, and apply a cooling period after mobile number or email changes.

title: Transaction fraud monitoring and limits
description: Monitor transactions in real time with documented fraud rules (velocity, geo-location, device, high-risk merchants, failed authentications), set and review transaction limits, staff a 24x7 fraud desk, and analyse the root cause of frauds.

title: Mobile and web payment application security
description: Protect customer apps with device binding, detection of rooted or tampered devices and remote-access apps, obfuscation, encrypted local storage, no stored credentials, forced upgrades of old versions, server-side checks for genuine apps, and takedown of rogue apps and phishing sites.

title: Payment system data stored only in India
description: Store all payment system data (end-to-end transaction details and customer data collected for payments) only in India, delete any copy processed abroad within the permitted time, and report compliance (with a system audit) as RBI requires.

title: Customer protection and grievance redressal
description: Give customers secure-usage guidance, an easy in-app and web route to report fraud and raise complaints, a named grievance officer and escalation matrix, online dispute resolution and refund timelines, and disclose risks and charges before they sign up.

title: Payment reconciliation and settlement controls
description: Reconcile transactions with banks, networks and merchants daily (settlement files within 24 hours of receipt), keep customer funds in the designated escrow or nodal account with only permitted credits and debits, and resolve differences on time.

title: Merchant and partner onboarding due diligence
description: Verify merchants and partners before onboarding (KYC, background checks, security assessment of their integration), monitor their transactions against their business profile, and offboard those that breach requirements.

title: Regulator-mandated IT governance committees and CISO independence
description: Run the IT Strategy Committee, IT Steering Committee and Information Security Committee at the required frequency and composition, and keep the CISO independent of the Head of IT and free of business targets, reporting cyber risk to the Board or its committee at least quarterly.

title: Information security policy
description: Maintain a top-level information security policy approved by management, published to all staff and reviewed at least annually.

title: ISMS scope and context
description: Document the organisation's context, interested parties and their requirements, and the scope and boundaries of the security programme.

title: Leadership oversight and management review
description: Leadership reviews the security programme at least annually, covering performance, risks, audit results and improvements, and records decisions.

title: Security roles and responsibilities
description: Define and assign security and privacy roles (security lead, DPO or privacy contact, control owners) with a documented responsibility matrix.

title: Segregation of duties
description: Identify conflicting duties (for example, approving and deploying the same change) and separate them or add compensating review.

title: Security objectives, resources and planning
description: Set measurable security objectives with owners and deadlines, allocate resources, and plan changes to the programme.

title: Document control and operating procedures
description: Control security documents with versioning, approval and access rules, and document key operating procedures.

title: Code of conduct
description: Publish a code of conduct covering ethics and integrity, acknowledged by all staff at joining and annually.

title: Internal security communication
description: Communicate security policies, objectives, changes and how to raise concerns to staff through regular channels.

title: External security and privacy commitments
description: Communicate security commitments to customers and partners through terms, a trust page and contractual documents, and keep them consistent with practice.

title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact
description: Keep a current list of authority contacts (CERT-In, Data Protection Board, sector regulator, police cyber cell), designate a CERT-In Point of Contact, and maintain memberships of security interest groups.

title: Legal and regulatory requirements register
description: Maintain a register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations (DPDP, CERT-In, IT Act, sector rules, customer contracts) and of software licences.

title: Internal audit and compliance checks
description: Run an internal audit programme with impartial auditors, and periodically check compliance with security policies and standards.

title: Security metrics and monitoring of the programme
description: Define and track security metrics (open vulnerabilities, training completion, access review completion) and report them to leadership.

title: Corrective action and continual improvement
description: Track nonconformities and control failures to root cause and corrective action, and verify actions are effective.

title: Security in projects and change initiatives
description: Include a security and privacy review in project kick-off and in significant business changes.

title: Competence for security roles
description: Define required competence for security and privacy roles and keep records of qualifications and training.

title: Board-level oversight of IT and cyber risk
description: A board committee (or the board itself) oversees IT strategy and cyber risk, meets on a fixed schedule, reviews the cyber risk posture and major incidents, and records its decisions.

title: Background verification
description: Run background checks proportionate to the role before joining, in line with applicable law.

title: Employment terms and confidentiality agreements
description: Include security and confidentiality obligations in employment and contractor agreements, signed before access is granted.

title: Security and privacy awareness training
description: Train all staff on security and DPDP privacy obligations at joining and annually, with role-based training for engineers.

title: Disciplinary process
description: Maintain a communicated disciplinary process for security and privacy policy violations.

title: Offboarding and return of assets
description: On exit, recover devices and assets, revoke access, and remind leavers of ongoing confidentiality duties.

title: Remote working security
description: Define security rules for remote work (secure networks, device use, no printing of confidential data) and enforce them technically where possible.

title: Security event reporting by staff
description: Give staff a simple channel to report suspected incidents and phishing, and make sure reports are triaged.

title: Incident response plan
description: Maintain and test an incident response plan with roles, severity levels, triage, containment, communication and regulator reporting steps.

title: CERT-In reporting within 6 hours
description: Report reportable cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them, using the prescribed format, and keep proof of submission.

title: Personal data breach notification
description: On a personal data breach, inform affected Data Principals and the Data Protection Board without delay, and submit the detailed report to the Board within 72 hours.

title: Post-incident review
description: Run a post-incident review for significant incidents and track improvement actions.

title: Evidence preservation
description: Preserve logs and forensic evidence during incidents with chain of custody.

title: Financial regulator incident reporting
description: Report cyber incidents to your financial sector regulator within its deadline (RBI through DAKSH or the PSO format, SEBI, IRDAI or IFSCA, usually within 6 hours of detection), send follow-up and root-cause reports when due, and keep proof of every submission.

title: Centralised logging with retention in India
description: Collect security and access logs from all ICT systems centrally, protect them from tampering, and retain them for at least one year within India (meets CERT-In 180 days and DPDP one year).

title: Security monitoring and alerting
description: Monitor logs and systems for suspicious activity with defined alerts, triage and escalation.

title: Clock synchronisation (NIC / NPL NTP)
description: Synchronise all system clocks to NTP sources traceable to NIC or NPL (for example time.nplindia.org or samay1.nic.in) so log timestamps are reliable.

title: Network security and segmentation
description: Restrict inbound access with firewalls or security groups, segment production from other networks, and block public exposure of storage and databases.

title: Encryption in transit
description: Encrypt data in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher for external and internal traffic carrying personal or confidential data.

title: Malware protection
description: Run endpoint protection or EDR on all laptops and servers, with alerts monitored.

title: Vulnerability management
description: Scan infrastructure, containers and dependencies for vulnerabilities and fix them within defined timelines (for example critical 15 days, high 30 days).

title: Penetration testing
description: Commission an independent penetration test at least annually (CERT-In empanelled auditor where required) and track findings to closure.

title: Secure configuration baselines
description: Apply hardened configuration baselines (for example CIS benchmarks) to cloud, servers and endpoints, control software installation, and detect drift.

title: Capacity management
description: Monitor capacity and performance with alerts and autoscaling to meet availability commitments.

title: Backups and restore testing
description: Back up critical data and systems automatically, encrypt and store backups separately, and test restores at least quarterly.

title: Redundancy and high availability
description: Design critical systems with redundancy (multi-AZ, failover) to meet availability targets.

title: Data masking and test data
description: Do not use real personal data in non-production environments unless masked or synthetic.

title: Data leakage prevention
description: Apply controls to prevent leakage of sensitive data, such as email and cloud storage sharing restrictions and DLP rules.

title: Web filtering
description: Block access to known malicious websites through DNS or endpoint filtering.

title: Cardholder data environment scope and segmentation
description: Document every system, network and process that stores, processes or transmits cardholder data or can affect its security, keep a data-flow diagram, segment the cardholder data environment and confirm the scope at least every 12 months.

title: Protection of stored account data
description: Keep stored card data to a minimum with a retention limit, never store sensitive authentication data after authorisation, mask PAN when displayed and render it unreadable wherever stored (tokenisation, truncation or strong encryption).

title: Approved Scanning Vendor and internal vulnerability scans
description: Run internal vulnerability scans and external scans by a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor at least once every three months and after significant changes, and rescan until passing.

title: Physical access control
description: Protect offices and secure areas with perimeter controls, badge or biometric entry, visitor logs and monitoring. For cloud-hosted systems, rely on the provider's attestations.

title: Environmental protection and equipment maintenance
description: Protect equipment from fire, water, power and cabling threats, and maintain it. For cloud infrastructure, review the provider's attestation.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
description: Enforce automatic screen lock and clear desk rules for confidential information.

title: Personal data inventory (record of processing)
description: Maintain an inventory of personal data processing activities with data categories, purposes, lawful ground, systems, processors, retention and transfers.

title: Privacy notice
description: Publish a standalone, itemised privacy notice in English and relevant Scheduled languages, with links to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board, and notify pre-Act users.

title: Consent capture and records
description: Capture specific, informed consent through a clear affirmative action, limited to necessary data, and keep records of notice version, purpose and timestamp.

title: Consent withdrawal
description: Let users withdraw consent as easily as they gave it, and stop processing (including by processors) within a defined time.

title: Legitimate use register
description: For processing without consent, record which legitimate use under Section 7 applies and the justification.

title: Data accuracy
description: Keep personal data accurate and complete where used for decisions or disclosed, with ways for users to update it.

title: Retention and erasure
description: Define retention periods per purpose, erase data (and have processors erase it) when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn, and give 48 hours' notice before erasure where the Rules require.

title: DPO or privacy contact published
description: Publish the contact details of the DPO or designated privacy person on the website and app, and include them in every response to a Data Principal.

title: Data principal rights and grievance handling
description: Publish how to make requests, verify identity, and handle access, correction, erasure, nomination and grievance requests within the response time (maximum 90 days for grievances).

title: Cross-border transfer assessment
description: Track where personal data is stored and accessed outside India, check against restricted country notifications and sectoral localisation rules.

title: Privacy by design and organisational measures
description: Embed privacy review in product design and maintain organisational measures (owners, procedures, reviews) that make DPDP obligations work in practice.

title: Risk assessment
description: Assess security and privacy risks at least annually and on significant change, using a documented method with risk owners and acceptance criteria.

title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
description: Decide treatment for each risk, maintain a Statement of Applicability, and track the treatment plan to completion with risk owner approval.

title: Fraud risk assessment
description: Consider fraud scenarios (misuse of access, false reporting, payment fraud) as part of the risk assessment.

title: Change impact assessment
description: Assess the security impact of significant changes to the business, technology or vendors before they happen.

title: Threat intelligence
description: Subscribe to threat feeds (for example CERT-In advisories) and act on relevant threats.

title: Secure development lifecycle
description: Define secure development rules, including security requirements, threat modelling for major features, and secure architecture principles.

title: Code review and branch protection
description: Require peer review and passing checks before merging to main branches, enforced through branch protection.

title: Automated security testing
description: Run dependency scanning, static analysis and secret scanning in CI, and fix findings by severity.

title: Environment separation
description: Separate development, staging and production environments and accounts, with restricted production access.

title: Change management
description: Track, test and approve changes to production, with emergency change procedures and rollback.

title: Outsourced development oversight
description: Apply the same security requirements, reviews and testing to code built by contractors and agencies.

title: Audit testing on production systems
description: Plan and approve audit and security tests on production systems to avoid disruption.

title: Vendor risk management
description: Keep a vendor inventory with risk tiers, assess vendors before onboarding and periodically by tier, and track their security posture.

title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements
description: Sign contracts with security requirements and a data processing agreement before sharing personal data with a processor, including breach notice, erasure and security safeguard obligations.

title: Cloud service security
description: Define how cloud services are selected, configured, monitored and exited, including shared responsibility and data location.

title: Outsourcing register, sub-contracting and exit plans
description: Keep a register of all outsourcing arrangements with materiality and criticality, approve sub-contracting in advance, and keep a tested exit plan for each material arrangement so data can be returned or destroyed and the service moved without disruption.
